newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 30.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones rose 84.66 points to 6,740.74. PLDT's ADR gained $1 to $59.50.
* The peso closed weaker at 26.343 to a U.S. dollar from 26.340.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index jumped 31.62 points to 3,373.61.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 10.53125 percent.
* The Philippine Senate and House of Representatives decided on Wednesday to end a month-long deadlock over the 1997 national budget, lawmakers said.

* The Philippines on Wednesday reported gross national product growth of 6.8 percent in 1996, which it said was within forecast ranges. Socio-Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito told reporters, however, that gross domestic growth in 1996 was below target at 5.5 percent.
The country had forecast 1996 GNP growth at 6.5-7.5 percent and GDP growth at between 6.0-6.8 percent.
* Philippine composite index fleetingly surged to 3,376.51 points on Wednesday, breaking the all time high of 3,375.94 level reached last July. The index later closed at 3,373.61 points, up 31.62.
Analysts said the stock market was gearing to break more records on the back of good company earnings and stron g economic performance.
*San Miguel Corp reported a net income of 6.09 billion pesos in 1996, up four percent from 5.84 billion in the previous year.

But the 1996 figure was bolstered by extraordinary gains coming from the sale of certain assets and a second-quarter write-back of 561 million pesos of provisions made in previous years, SMC said in a statement.
Excluding the extraordinary gains, San Miguel's 1996 net income declined by two percent to 5.26 billion pesos from 5.38 billion in 1995, or to 2.57 pesos per share from 2.63, the company said.
*The Philippines' fiscal surplus for 1996 fell to 6.256 billion pesos from 11.074 billion.
* Alliad Banking Corp generated a net income of 1.039 billion pesos in 1996 versus 922.3 million in the previous year, the company said in a statement on Wednesday.
